learningObjective: Reason about the sources of cold-start cost (compile, load, warmup) and how compilation caches reduce them across process restarts.
stem: Which statements about cold-start cost and compilation caches for compiled ML workloads are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Cold-start cost consists of several distinct phases: process init (import framework, load driver), model artifact load (weights, graph), possibly compilation (JIT lowering), and warmup (autotune, cuBLAS handle init, kernel loading). Each has a different mitigation strategy.

A compilation cache stores previously compiled kernels or lowered graphs keyed by (source, shape/dtype/device, compiler-version) and hits skip the compile phase on subsequent process starts; a properly warm cache can turn a multi-minute torch.compile cold start into a fraction of that.
AOT-compiled artifacts (TensorRT plan, AOTInductor .so) eliminate the JIT compile phase entirely at cold start because compilation happened offline; process init and weight load costs still remain.

Compilation caches guarantee that a cached hit produces exactly the same output tensors as a fresh compile; any bitwise difference between cached and fresh outputs is a compiler bug that must be fixed before shipping.

explanation: A: cold-start is multi-phase and mitigations target each phase differently. B: compilation caches (Inductor cache, cuDNN autotune cache, TVM cache) key on inputs and skip lowering on hits. C: AOT eliminates the JIT step, though process init and weight load remain. D is wrong: cached and fresh compilations can produce different low-order-bit numerics if kernel selection or algorithm choice differs between the two paths — this is not necessarily a bug, particularly for cuBLAS/cuDNN autotune caches where algorithm selection can be non-deterministic across runs.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: compilation caches deliver large cold-start savings.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: AOT removes JIT from the cold path.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: bitwise equivalence between cached and fresh compilations is not guaranteed.

assumptions: A production system where cold-start latency (SLI/SLO) matters.
The runtime supports some form of compilation caching.
nonImplications: Does not imply caches are always safe across framework upgrades; version keys are essential to avoid stale hits.
Does not imply cache misses can be ignored; the first request after cache invalidation still pays the full cold-start cost.

sourceRefs.locator: AOTInductor deployment: zero JIT cost at start
